title: 'Angel in rhinestones'; FOX8's Chad Tucker reflects on Dolly Parton's impact on his family - NewsBreak
text:
By Justyn Araya-DeBusk ,
1 hours ago
(WGHP) — Dolly Parton, the nationally beloved singer-songwriter, actress and entrepreneur, touched countless lives, including the family of FOX8's own Chad Tucker, who experienced her kindness in person twice.
Chad and his family first met Parton during the weekend kick-off for Dollywood's 39th season in 2024.
He said his youngest daughter, Pearl Monroe Tucker, also known affectionately as Roe Roe, had survived an 858-day battle with Leukemia, and she held up a sign that read, "Dolly, your music helped me beat cancer."
FOX8's Chad Tucker's daughters meet Dolly Parton during Dollywood's 39th opening weekend (WGHP) FOX8's Chad Tucker's daughters meet Dolly Parton during Dollywood's 39th opening weekend (WGHP) FOX8's Chad Tucker's daughters meet Dolly Parton during Dollywood's 39th opening weekend (WGHP) "And she held it up, just wanting Dolly to see it, but of course, Dolly and her big heart stopped to say hello," Chad said. "I'll never forget her saying to her that she was just so happy for her, and also complimented her beautiful dresses there, her and her sister. But, she was just so sweet and down-home for that, to take time to speak with her and just tell her how happy she was."
Chad told her about how much his daughters admire "The Book Lady," a name garnered from the singer's founding of The Imagination Library . Inspired by Dolly's Imagination Library, the Tucker family started "The Hero Library" through Roe Roe's Heroes Childhood Cancer Foundation .
Chad explained that Dolly's music and books helped when his daughter was going through chemotherapy and steroids.
"[The steroids] would just really have her go into 'roid rage' as people call it, and the music would help calm her down, us reading to her would help calm her down," Chad said.
A year later, in 2025, Chad and his family returned for the opening of Dollywood's 40th season. It was during that weekend that Dolly spotted them and waved. A moment later, he said Dolly's nephew found them and brought them to see the singer .
Dolly Parton (center) meets Chad Tucker's daughters Carson Parry (left) and Pearl Monroe (righ). (Chad Tucker/WGHP) Dolly Parton (center left) meets Chad Tucker's children Carson Parry (far left), Pearl Monroe (center right) and Franklin Reeves (far right). (Chad Tucker/WGHP) Chad Tucker (left) and his wife Meredith (right) meet Dolly Parton (center). (Chad Tucker/WGHP) Chad Tucker (back left), his wife Meredith (back right) and their children Carson Parry (front left), Pearl Monroe (front center) and Franklin Reeves (front right) meet Dolly Parton (back center). (Chad Tucker/WGHP) "She remembered the girls," Chad said. "... She said,' I've met you before, and one of y'all was sick.' And so, we got to meet her again, and just the fact that, of all the people she meets, you know, she still remembered these two little girls outside of the hotel there. And, it was just really powerful for someone like her to take time to speak to us and speak to the girls. And again, she felt like at home when you were talking to her."
According to Chad, Roe Roe had said hugging Dolly was "like hugging an angel in rhinestones."
